title: Dialysis dependence and long-term outcome after cardiac surgery using a heart-lung machine: a multicenter observational study
summary: The incidence of moderate and severe acute kidney injury (AKI) requiring postoperative dialysis after cardiac surgery under cardiopulmonary bypass varies depending on preoperative risk factors such as pre-existing renal insufficiency, the duration of cardiopulmonary bypass, the type of cardiac surgery, and between different study centers. Patients with moderate and severe AKI are more likely to experience adverse serious renal and cardiovascular events and have increased mortality.
conditions: Acute renal failure with tubular necrosis

interventions.name:
Patients with AKI stage ≥2 and a history of cardiac surgery in the cardiopulmonary bypass monitoring group
Metadata collection during enrollment (age, sex, comorbidities, type of surgery, etc.)
Follow-up with recording of mortality, MAKE (major adverse kidney events) and MACE (major adverse cardia

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients ≥ 18 years of age with a history of cardiac surgery (elective or emergency) using cardiopulmonary bypass and AKI stage ≥2
Exclusion criteria:
any renal replacement therapy (chronic renal insufficiency stage G5d: hemodialysis, peritoneal dialysis), kidney transplantation
